newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bank says Italians seek bigger stake.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bank says Italians seek bigger stake.

text.p: Polnobanka a.s., Slovakia's fourth largest commercial bank, on Wednesday said it had asked the central bank for approval to allow its two Italian partners to increase their holdings up to a total 15 percent.

"At the request of our Italian partners - Unicredito and Finest - we have asked the central bank to approve an increase of their holdings to around 7.0 to 7.5 percent (each)," Polnobanka General Director Ludovit Posa said.
In early June, Unicredito S.p.A. and Finest S.p.A., two north Italian regional investment groups, took 2.6 and 2.8 percent stakes respectively in Polnobanka.

Posa said the capital entry of Italian partners, the first Italian banking investment in Slovakia, would strengthen the bank's capital efficiency and widen its commercial sphere, especially in the framework of Slovak-Italian commercial relations.
In June Polnobanka shareholders also approved a 600 million crown increase of basic capital to 1.85 billion through a share issue with prepurchase rights for current shareholders.

The bank's main shareholders are Slovenska Poistovna, the country's largest insurer (31.9 percent), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (20 percent), and the Slovak agriculture ministry (8.6 percent).
About 20 percent of Polnobanka shares are held by other small shareholders.
The two Italian groups originally accumlated their stakes through purchases from small shareholders, but did not specify how they planned to increase their stakes.
